requirements.requirement: Inventory web application running on node2, listening on port 8080
requirements.summary: inventory-app.service created, enabled, and active on node2; /healthz returns ok/server=node2. Confirmed in final after_executor listening-sockets snapshot showing 0.0.0.0:8080 bound by python3.

requirements.requirement: Inventory web application running on node3, listening on port 8080
requirements.summary: inventory-app.service created, enabled, and active on node3; /healthz returns ok/server=node3. Confirmed in final after_executor listening-sockets snapshot showing 0.0.0.0:8080 bound by python3.

requirements.requirement: node1 load-balances incoming HTTP requests across both backends on port 80
requirements.summary: nginx installed and configured on node1 with an upstream block round-robining between node2 and node3 on 8080, listening on port 80. Repeated curl loops against node1 port 80 show responses alternating cleanly between node2 and node3. after_executor listening-sockets confirms nginx bound to 0.0.0.0:80 on node1.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task were satisfied and directly verified: inventory-app.service is active on node2 and node3 on port 8080, and nginx on node1 round-robins HTTP traffic on port 80 across both backends, confirmed via repeated alternating curl responses and final listening-socket snapshots. The executor also completed the provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on all three nodes: each node's pre-restart boot_id and healthy service state, the systemctl reboot acknowledgement, a changed post-restart boot_id, and recovered service/LB state were all directly captured, and these boot_id transitions are independently corroborated by the fixed before_prepare and after_executor lifecycle snapshots. Minor hygiene issue: one failed sed-based config edit was quickly self-corrected, leaving a small unremoved backup file but no functional residue.
limitations: The nginx.conf.orig backup file's final on-disk presence was not explicitly re-verified after the corrected edit, so minor residue is inferred rather than directly confirmed present or absent.
Package-health checks only report the package manager in use rather than a full consistency/integrity result, limiting confidence in that specific hygiene dimension.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands were largely purposeful: installing nginx, writing the inventory app, configuring systemd units, opening firewall ports, and enabling the SELinux boolean httpd_can_network_connect all had clear causal roles in satisfying the task or fixing a real blocking issue (502s from SELinux denial, confirmed via error.log). One troubleshooting misstep occurred: cmd-35a6cfdb13544afb attempted to comment out the default nginx server block with an incorrect sed line range, producing an invalid config (nginx -t failed). This was immediately caught and reverted by restoring from a backup (cmd-5edada88490c4073) before a corrected sed range was applied successfully (cmd-c540f62c31d34262). This was a bounded, low-risk, self-corrected mutation with no lasting negative effect. A leftover /etc/nginx/nginx.conf.orig backup file was not explicitly cleaned up, representing minor, benign residue. No failed or conflicting services and no weakened security posture were observed in the final state.
